title: The Pulse, Thursday 29 October 2026
tldr: Gemini 4 Carbon launched with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. OpenAI will give Pro and Business subscribers up to $500/month in API credits for building agents. Node 26 enters LTS as Lithium.

models.title: Particle AI: Particle-1
models.summary: Token-efficient agentic coding model post-trained on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 1M context, $0.25/$1 per million tokens.
models.why: Another coding agent option at competitive pricing, worth evaluating against Claude and GPT-4 for terminal workflows and codebase changes.

models.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model
models.summary: Google's strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities (848 points and 705 comments on HN).
models.why: Cybersecurity capabilities matter for reviewing client code, and long-horizon reasoning helps with multi-step agent workflows.

releases.title: Node.js 26.13.0 'Lithium' (LTS)
releases.summary: Node 26 transitions to Long Term Support with the codename Lithium, supported through April 2029. Separately, Node 24.22.2 shipped with V8 backports and a stream fix for async context.
releases.why: Our primary runtime for services across SalesKick, Pipeline, and Botterfly; Node 26 LTS means we can upgrade confidently, and the Node 24 stream fix matters for Pipeline's event-driven flows.

releases.title: LangChain Core 1.7.1
releases.summary: Gateway tracing metadata preserved in v3 streams, Mermaid label escaping fix, relaxed third-party dependency bounds.
releases.why: We use LangChain for retrieval pipelines; tracing fixes help with debugging agent workflows.

hackernews.title: The Agent SDK
hackernews.summary: Cursor's SDK for building agents, 109 points and 116 comments.
hackernews.why: We build coding agents; Cursor's approach to agent APIs is worth studying for our own tooling.

hackernews.title: Dayjob: Tax – evaluating AI agents on 50 professional tax assignments
hackernews.summary: Benchmark evaluating agents on real professional tax work, 217 points and 139 comments.
hackernews.why: Real-world agent benchmarks help us calibrate expectations for our own agent deployments.

hackernews.title: Qwenputer: A functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5
hackernews.summary: Someone implemented a working RISC-V CPU using Qwen's transformer weights, 208 points.
hackernews.why: No direct use for us yet, but shows how far the interpretability-through-engineering frontier has moved.

hackernews.title: StackOverflow now gets fewer than 1000 questions a month
hackernews.summary: Stack Overflow question volume has collapsed to under 1000/month, 211 points.
hackernews.why: Confirms the shift to LLM-first development; affects how we onboard engineers and expect them to learn.

hackernews.title: Nvidia Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe: open ASR for 40 languages
hackernews.summary: Open multilingual ASR model from Nvidia, 116 points.
hackernews.why: EverRaise voice agents need accurate ASR; another option beyond what we're using on Vapi.

x_posts.title: OpenAI API credits for ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers
x_posts.summary: ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers can now claim up to $500/month in API credits for building apps and agents.
x_posts.why: We're building agents on OpenAI; $500/month reduces our API costs if we migrate agent development to those accounts.

x_posts.title: Mistral Responses API
x_posts.summary: Mistral's new Responses API separates the model's answer, reasoning, and tool calls for easier agent building.
x_posts.why: Structured agent responses make tooling cleaner; worth evaluating for our DSPy and LangChain pipelines.

x_posts.title: Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3
x_posts.summary: Ranks #2 on Voice Arena's Diarization + ASR leaderboard.
x_posts.why: EverRaise voice agents need accurate ASR; a competitive alternative to what we're using on Vapi.

x_posts.title: Automating code reviews
x_posts.summary: Santiago argues everyone should focus on automating code reviews since agents can write infinite code but it's useless if it doesn't work.
x_posts.why: Directly relevant to our wehshi PR review panel; validates the investment in adversarial multi-model review.

closing: Research: arXiv returned zero papers in the window.
